pr_title: extensions: Select language extension based on longest matching path extension
pr_body:
This is a "let's see if I can get it to work" (aka hack) to try address #8408 and #10997. In short: the [current language extension matcher](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/language/src/language_registry.rs#L511-L520) is only considering the "final extension" of a file when seeing which language extensions would apply to the file. (This is because that's how Rust's `path.extension()` works.) This works fine for most cases, but there are some cases where a language extension may want to match on a "compound file extension", and this is currently not supported at all. 

**Example:**
- Laravel Blade templates use the `blade.php` "extension"
- So a Blade file may be named `index.blade.php`
- [A hypothetical](https://github.com/claytonrcarter/zed-language-laravel-blade) lang extension for Blade will specify `path_suffixes = ["blade.php"]`
- Zed will look at `index.blade.php`, and then try to match a lang ext based on any of the `path_suffixes` exactly matching [either `"php"` or `"index.blade.php"`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/language/src/language_registry.rs#L511-L513)
- The Blade ext will not match because `"blade.php" != "php"` nor `"index.blade.php"`

**Proposed Solution**
Basically, instead of doing an exact match on the suffix and either the file extension or filename, this change:
- finds the longest suffix that matches the end of the filename
- returns the suffix string length as the matching "score"

**Languages that may use this**
- Laravel Blade templates use the `blade.php` "extension"
- I'm not familiar with Angular, but apparently it [uses `component.html`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/10765#issuecomment-2091293304)
- *others?*

**Open questions**
- perf: I'm assuming that `filename.ends_with(&ext) || filename == suffix` is slower than `path_suffixes.contains(&Some(suffix.as_str()))`? If so, how bad is it?
  - alternate option: separate `path_suffixes` in the ext API into `path_suffixes` and `filenames`, and then we could preprocess these when the language ext is first loaded to reduce overhead
- ~~unintended matches: I realized while writing this that it may introduce behavior where (eg) a lang ext for D (suffix `d`) may be matched to Markdown (`md`). In that case, Markdown would still win, though (because of length) ... so may that's not an issue?~~ **edit** I resolved this when I found the tests that cover this change and go this to pass.
- alternate approach: perhaps declare within an extension that it may "compete" with other extensions and provide some way to disambiguate which should apply?
- prior art: #10960 is related to this, but I believe that it is addressing a different problem

Release Notes:

- Added support for "compound" file extensions in language extensions. Fixes #8408 and #10997.

issue_context.title: Reconcile multiple language match by suffix length
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

Inspired by https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/7096#issuecomment-1948414691.

# The problem
Today, when multiple `LanguageMatcher`'s path_suffix match a file,  one random language will be chosen (see [language_registry.rs get_or_load_language function](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ffdda588b41f7d9d270ffe76cab116f828ad545e/crates/language/src/language_registry.rs#L347-L358)). While this simple setting works well for most of the cases, it's not robust enough. E.g. there's no way to distinguish `.php` or `.blade.php`.

# Proposed fix
To make it simple, I propose changing [the callback function](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ffdda588b41f7d9d270ffe76cab116f828ad545e/crates/language/src/language_registry.rs#L342) so that it returns a tuple of boolean + max matched suffix length among all the suffixes. When there're multiple matches, the language with the longest suffix wins.


### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


_No response_
comments: I agree this would be a clear improvement. In PR #11697, @claytonrcarter did a bit of work trying to implement it. If anyone has the time to finish up that work, that would be great.

> In PR [#11697](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/11697), [@claytonrcarter](https://github.com/claytonrcarter) did a bit of work trying to implement it. If anyone has the time to finish up that work, that would be great.

Thanks for the shout out, Max. I obviously haven't been able to get back to #11697, but I have at least been keeping the code rebased and building. If anyone wants to pick it up, feel free to use the code at https://github.com/claytonrcarter/zed/tree/extension-length as a starting point, if you'd like. As I recall, when I left it, I had resolved most of the review comments, but glob support had recently been added and I got stumped on how globs should factor in to "length of matched suffix length". I believe that the code in the above branch just counts the string length of the glob as if it were a static suffix (ie `*js` = 3 and `js` = 2) ... that is probably fine for most cases, but I just haven't had time to get back to double check and to polish it again for a PR.

review_comments: Oops, I forgot to update this like I did above to support the full file name and prevent (eg) `rs` also matching `.cars`. I'll leave this as is for now, pending input from someone else on how to proceed. 😄

Yeah, I think we should use the same logic for finding the suffix length, for both the default path suffixes and the user-defined path suffixes.

I'd write it something like this:

```rs
let matching_suffix_len = config
    .path_suffixes
    .iter()
    .filter(|suffix| {
        filename == suffix ||
            filename.strip_suffix(suffix).map_or(false, |prefix| prefix.ends_with('.'))
    })
    .map(|suffix| suffix.len())
    .max();
```
I used `MAX` to ensure that user overrides always win.
I don't think the user override needs to *always* win. I think we could use the longest match, but in the event of a tie, favor the user-defined path suffix.
One way to implement that is to multiple the longest matching suffix's length by *two* and then add one if it's a user-defined suffix. Curious what you think of that.
